about: The frigate's head and stern decoration (docs/shipkit-9): the knee of the head and its cheeks, trailboards, rails, timbers and gratings, the knightheads and the bow's opening for the bowsprit, the gammoning and bobstays, our figurehead, the stern's windows, carvings, name, taffrail and quarter pieces, the quarter galleries and the stern lanterns. Metres in the ship's frame (X forward, Y starboard, Z up, origin on the centreline at midships on waterline A) unless a key says ft or in. Starboard parts are mirrored for port.

sources.lines_1927: NARA 1927 lines plan of Constitution (refs.json): the head's profile in elevation, traced at the centre of the ink and taken to the ship's frame by scanreg (drawing_1927.json): the cutwater, the cheeks, the main head rail and the upper rail; the stern's taffrail, galleries and windows in the body plan's stern view
sources.draught_1817: the 1817 draught of a 44 (refs.json): the head's rails and figure, the quarter gallery's five lights, its carved roof and drop
sources.practice: the period's practice for a large frigate (by eye where no drawing gives it, each so marked)

head.note: Our bowsprit steeves from the forecastle (slice 3), about 1.3 m higher at the stem than the 1927 plan's, so the knee, cheeks and main rail keep the plan's elevation and the figure stands up into the room under the bowsprit; the rails' forward ends rise to her back

knee.cutwater_src: lines_1927: the cutwater's fore edge, from the waterline up to the figure's seat
knee.top_src: by eye: the knee's upper edge from the figure's seat aft to the stem head, dipping between them (the head's lacing), so the gammoning's legs and the sky show under the bowsprit
knee.siding_src: practice: sided a little less than the stem (0.46 m with its rabbet) and tapering forward
knee.bevel_src: practice: the cutwater's fore edge is taken down to about half the knee's siding over its last 9 cm

gammoning.src: practice: seven to nine turns of 6 in rope through a slot in the knee just forward of the stem, leading forward over the bowsprit, frapped in the middle (the frapping draws each side's legs half way in)

bobstays.src: practice: two bobstays for a 44, each doubled through a hole in the cutwater close in from its fore edge (its middle 0.18 m in), its parts coming together forward of the edge, set up with deadeyes and a lanyard to a collar on the bowsprit, the lower hole's stay to the outer collar so they never cross. Practice puts the holes below the lower cheek, but our bowsprit steeves 1.3 m higher than the 1927 plan's and a stay from there would lie along the knee's raked fore edge for 3 m: they are in the cutwater's upright part over the trailboards' forward end, where the stays leave the edge within 0.4 m. The collars: the inner between the bowsprit shrouds' outer collar and the spritsail yard's sling, the outer between the fore stay's collar and the cap; the stays clear the figure, her console and the spritsail yard

knightheads.src: practice: a timber either side of the bowsprit over the stem head, rising about 18 in over the rail cap, closed in to the spar (an inch or less either side); the bow's bulwark opened between them down to the bowsprit's bed (Head.open_bow)

bed.src: practice: the bowsprit bedded on the stem head, the bed hollowed to the spar's round (here the lower half of a 32-sided polygon about it, clear_m under it) and filling between the knightheads under it; its bottom depth_m under the hollow's lowest line, its faces lap_m outside the bow's planking and inside face, fore_m short of the stem's fore face, side_m inside the knightheads and the stem's sides

cheeks.src: lines_1927: the two cheeks' bands as traced (their middles), from the bow onto the knee; sizes by practice (a 44's cheeks about 9 in deep, standing 7 in off the side); their backs fayed to the bow, the stem and the knee (let in embed_m), their fore ends stopped with every point fore_clear_m short of the cutwater's edge

trailboard.src: practice: a carved board between the cheeks on each side of the knee, from the stem to the figure; its fore end short of the cutwater's edge, clear of the bobstay holes

carving.src: practice: a running scroll (a stem waving along the board, a branch from each wave curling back into the bay under its crest, with leaves) carved on the trailboards and gilt

rails.src: lines_1927: the main rail's after part as traced (its lower edge, the middle a half depth above), its after end brought in onto the bow and fayed to the planking under the cathead (fay_m, land_m: main, lower); its fore part raised to land on the figure's console under her heels (our bowsprit is higher); the lower rail (the gratings' edge) half a metre under it, after the 1817 draught's second rail; plan by practice (the head's sides flaring out to the bow)

timbers.src: practice: four head timbers a side, from the upper cheek up to the main rail

gratings.src: practice: the head gratings either side of the knee, a hand rail's height under the main rail: battens and ledges halved together with square openings, let into the knee's (aft, the stem's) side and the lower rail's inner face (let_in_m), their top top_under_rail_m under the rail's top

base.src: practice: the figure stands on a carved console (a bracket) on the knee's top, curled aft under her heels, its volutes gilt; its top a little over her footprint

figure.src: our figure: Thorvaldsen's Goddess of Hope (1817) from a scan (Zenodo 10242636, CC BY 4.0, Geoffrey Marchal), standing on a carved scroll at the knee's top under the bowsprit, leaning out with the head as figures of the 1790s did; a little over life size, as a 44's figure was
figure.colour_src: practice: painted white over the carving (the American frigates' figures were painted), her console with her, its volutes and bead gilt

stern.note: On the stern face things stand by (u, v): u across (m, + starboard), v up (m, the ship's z), on the transom as loft draws it (its round-up), off it along its normal. Heights are tied to the side's own lines where the 1927 plan's agree with them: the taffrail is the quarterdeck's rail, the ports stand between the spar port sill line and the sheer, the arch's top is at the plankshear

paint.src: practice: a black stern, the windows' casings and pilasters yellow ochre like the side's band, the sashes white, the carving gilt

taffrail.src: lines_1927: the stern's top rail at the quarterdeck's rail height (our rail cap's section, carried across from corner to corner, standing a little over the side caps' ends that run into it), a moulding across at the sheer (the plan's line at 19.5 ft) and the board between them

frieze.src: practice: the taffrail board carved with a running scroll in gilt, growing from a star on the middle line out to each quarter

ports.src: lines_1927: three ports in the stern's bulwark over the quarterdeck (one on the middle line, one each side 6.1 to 9.4 ft out), between the spar port sill line and the sheer as the side's are; shown closed, their lids hung from the top

arch.src: lines_1927: an arched band over the windows, level across at 15.4 to 15.9 ft (the plankshear's height on our side), its corners rounded about 3.5 ft, its legs close in to the stern's edge down to the name band (its feet stand on the band's top)

stars.src: lines_1927: a star over the middle window and one each side 9.7 ft out, between the windows and the arch

windows.src: lines_1927: the cabin's three windows, the middle one 4 ft wide, the others 4.4 to 8 ft out, each three panes by two, 9.8 to 12.5 ft over A; set 2 in higher, over the name band (see name)

pilasters.src: lines_1927: a pair of pilasters either side of each side window (2.5 and 3.85 ft, 9.0 and 11.3 ft out), each with a round boss over its capital

name.src: lines_1927: the name in capitals on a band across the stern under the windows (8.0 to 9.2 ft there); its foot raised 0.15 m, to stand clear of the rudder head where it comes up through the counter, its top 1 cm under the windows' sill (so 0.27 m deep, the letters 0.19 m). Libre Baskerville (SIL Open Font License 1.1: ../jclass/fonts/OFL-LibreBaskerville.txt), the glyphs made mesh; the font itself is not shipped

quarter_pieces.src: practice: a carved piece down each corner of the stern from the taffrail's end, over the side planking's ends, a volute under the taffrail

galleries.src: lines_1927 (sheer plan): a gallery on each quarter, raked with the stern, its lights 9.5 to 14.6 ft over A in three windows of two panes by three between pilasters, a cornice over them, a roof rising to the side, a base and a drop under them; draught_1817: the roof carved with rows of scales, a garland down its fore edge, the drop's leaves; a light in its after face (practice). Kept aft of the aftmost spar deck port: the roof drops to the cornice before it; 3.1 m long (the plan's 3.25 shortened to stand 4 cm clear of the mizzen's after chain), its roof falling from 1.4 m to clear the aftmost spar deck port's lining

cabin_window.src: lines_1927 (sheer plan): a glazed sash of six panes the size of a gun port, forward of the gallery (the cabin's side light); 1.02 m wide, centred between the mizzen's second and third chains (4 cm clear of each)

lanterns.src: practice (the 1817 draught shows one at the quarter): a lantern on an iron bracket off each quarter piece, aft of the stern's edge and just outboard of the taffrail's end, its top under the spanker boom's swing (the boom swung through its brace limits passes at least boom_clear_min_m over them)

meets.note: the head's and stern's parts that meet another part of the ship (or each other) by design, each pair with why and how far (in) either may go into the other; every other meeting fails the build (build_frigate's decor_room, deck.room). Each entry: the parts on one side, the parts on the other, why, the depth allowed: the deepest the build measures over the entry's pairs (deck.room's measure, how far a vertex lies behind the other's nearest face, found within 0.3 m, so never more than 11.8 in) with a quarter inch over, a guard against a part moving deeper. seated: the carving, laid on what it meets by design here; every piece of it must reach into that, and every open rim of a leaf or a berry lie in it (build_frigate's decor_seated, carve.seated)
pairs: the knee is fayed and bolted to the stem's fore face, the cheeks' after ends to its sides
the gratings' inner ends lie on the stem
the gratings are let into the knee's sides and the lower rails' inner faces
the cheeks are bolted to the knee's sides
the trailboard is let in between the cheeks
the head timbers stand on the upper cheeks and their feet on the knee
the rails' fore ends and the trailboard are let into the knee
the gammoning and the bobstays pass through the knee's holes
the cheeks are fayed to the bow's planking, their after ends tapering into it
the rails' after ends are fayed to the bow's planking, over its mouldings
the head timbers are let into the rails and carry the gratings
her cut base is let 1 cm into the console's top
the console stands on the knee's head, let into it
the main rails' fore ends run into the console's after curl, under her heels
the console's gilt bead and volutes laid on it
the carving is cut in the trailboard
the knightheads stand up through the forecastle's deck and the bow's opened bulwark, whose cut ends they cover
the bowsprit's bed lies down on the stem head between the knightheads, the bow's planking and its inside end on its top
the taffrail sits on the stern's top and the bulwark, over the side caps' ends
the spanker boom sheet block's eyebolt is driven into the taffrail, its eye half sunk in it
laid on the stern's face, their backs let in
the carved board's work cut in it and under the taffrail's cap; the beads along the arch and the name band
the sashes and their glass sit in the casings
the glass sits in the sash's rebates
the quarter pieces cover the planking's ends at the stern's corners and the stern's bands' ends
the galleries stand on the side, their backs let into the planking and over the mouldings that run on under them
the gallery's carving runs to the side where the gallery stands on it
the gallery's frames, sashes, glass and carving in and on its body, the drop's foot in its carved leaves
the gallery's sashes and glass in the after light's casing
the glass sits in the sash's rebates
the quarter piece runs down the gallery's after edge
the cabin's side light let into the side
the sash and its glass sit in the casing
the glass sits in the sash's rebates
the lantern's bracket is let into the quarter piece
the glass panes sit in the lantern's frame
